claims.text: An XGBoost-based data-driven framework can be used to select LPBF process conditions.
The XGBoost approach is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock.
The applicable LPBF laser-power window is 50–150 W.
The applicable scan-speed window is 800–1500 mm/s.
A layer thickness of approximately 20 μm is applicable.
Thermal-camera and melt-pool measurements can support rapid, real-time adjustment of LPBF parameters by the proposed framework.
Machine-learning optimization will minimize local overheating in AlCrFeNiSi LPBF.
Optimized heat input will reduce thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients will produce a refined and more uniform microstructure.
Reduced heat flux and thermal gradients will lessen residual-stress accumulation.
Lower residual-stress accumulation will diminish microstructural discontinuities and cracking.
Diminished discontinuities and cracking will preserve or enhance mechanical integrity.
Optimized miniature AlCrFeNiSi components will have residual stress below 50% of that in components made under conventional high-thermal-load conditions.
Optimized miniature AlCrFeNiSi components will have 5–10% higher mechanical strength than components made under conventional high-thermal-load conditions.
The proposed process is applicable to single-laser LPBF systems with machine power up to 150 W.
The proposed process is applicable to parts with cross-sections of approximately 5 mm or less and minimal geometric complexity.
The model may require recalibration for multi-laser systems, larger builds, different hardware, distinct feedstock batches, and other part geometries.
Prior work experimentally validated an XGBoost-based LPBF process-condition model on 316L stainless steel, AlSi10Mg, and Fe60Co15Ni15Cr10 powders.
The cited model predicted LPBF conditions yielding products with relative density greater than 98%.
